title: Bounded-influence allocation under adversarial demand claims

profile.cap_rule: claims capped at 2x or 4x lower median before discretionary allocation

claim_ceiling: Lower-median capping is not demand authentication or Sybil resistance. The attack sweep has stable identities, <=25% attacker shards and no identity churn. The honest hotspot sweep assumes a new allocation each epoch and does not model partitions or outstanding obligations. A zero lower median means no reliable relative scale exists; the bounded-cap policy therefore falls back to equal cold-start weights instead of deriving a cap only from positive claims.

execution_evidence.python_fixed_seed_allocation_sweep: 10000 cases in unit test; each checks stable-ID order independence and capacity conservation
execution_evidence.rust_build_tests_clippy: not_run; rustc/cargo unavailable in this environment

decision_rule: Do not select cap/floor from aggregate demand served alone. Evaluate joint honest-load and adversarial-load frontier, worst-shard service, Jain fairness, stranded rights, identity threat model and recovery correctness.
